one_liner: APIs for connecting apps to users' bank accounts and financial data.

evidence.claim: API authentication uses a client_id and secret pair (API-key style), sent in body or headers.
evidence.quote: Almost all Plaid API endpoints require a `client_id` and `secret`. These may be sent either in the request body or in the headers `PLAID-CLIENT-ID` and `PLAID-SECRET`.

evidence.claim: Credentials are self-serve: signing up on the Plaid Dashboard yields a live client_id and secret.
evidence.quote: To gain access to the Plaid API, create an account on the [Plaid Dashboard](https://dashboard.plaid.com/). Once you've completed the signup process and acknowledged our terms, we'll provide a live `client_id` and `secret` via the Dashboard.

evidence.claim: A free tier exists with free initial API calls.
evidence.quote: Build with our free tier; pay as you go; or scale with tailored API solutions and volume pricing. Your first 200 API calls are free.

evidence.claim: The API is REST-style JSON over HTTP with an OpenAPI spec.
evidence.quote: The Plaid API is JSON over HTTP. Requests are POST requests, and responses are JSON, with errors indicated in response bodies as `error_code` and `error_type`

evidence.claim: Plaid's official docs document an MCP server (Dashboard MCP, Streamable HTTP).
evidence.quote: The Dashboard MCP server is available at https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/ and uses the Streamable HTTP protocol.

notes: Sandbox credentials are fully self-serve, but Production API access must be requested via the Dashboard (approval step), and per-item product calls require a user-consented access_token obtained via the Link flow. The official MCP server is scoped to the Plaid Dashboard (account/team management), not the core financial-data API. Broad product surface: Auth, Balance, Identity, Transactions, Investments, Liabilities, Transfer, Identity Verification, and more. OpenAPI spec and Postman collection are published on Plaid's GitHub org.
